title: The platform: GPU pools, controllers, the rollout fleet and the network between them
purpose: Show what the experiments run on: which nodes and GPUs, which controllers, how the rollout fleet is laid out, and how fast the network between the trainer and the rollout nodes really is.

checks.description: one trainer GPU and two rollout GPUs are schedulable, all in one zone
checks.because: The NVIDIA device plugin advertises each GPU as nvidia.com/gpu. All three nodes are in one zone so weight transfer and rollouts never cross a zone boundary, which is billed in both directions.

checks.description: JobSet, LeaderWorkerSet and KEDA are installed
checks.because: JobSet restarts the trainer, LeaderWorkerSet runs the rollout fleet, KEDA scales the environment tier. Terraform installs them; the tests install only the workloads.

checks.description: the rollout fleet is two engines on two nodes behind one address
checks.because: vLLM runs one data-parallel engine per node: the leader pod serves the API and the worker pod joins headless. The trainer talks to the leader only, and the weight-transfer group spans both engines.

checks.description: the trainer-to-rollout network was measured, not assumed
checks.because: iperf3 sends from a pod on the trainer node to a pod on a rollout node with four parallel streams for fifteen seconds. The result sizes every weight push in S05; the design tells us to size it like a serving path.
